messages:
anya: Heads-up — I just noticed a staging worker printed an API key in a debug log while testing a new retry path. Only in staging, not prod, but still. Can we confirm the correct emergency rotation steps + who needs to approve?

mike: rotate immediately and revoke old key. staging only reduces blast radius but still treat as compromised. Steps we usually follow: 1) create new key in Vault/KMS 2) update deploy/staging secret 3) restart service 4) revoke old key.

anya: thanks. quick Q — do we prefer creating the key in Vault (kv v2) or in cloud KMS with wrapped key material? staging is on our cloud acct with Vault integrated.

mike: either is fine for staging. For short-lived staging keys: Vault kv v2 is easiest: put a new secret version and update the env var. For long-term/cert-like keys or if hardware-backed protection needed, import into HSM or use KMS-wrapped keys.

security-ops: @anya please open a security-incident ticket in #incidents with "staging key leak" prefix and paste the leaked blob (redact actual key if you're adding screenshots). For approvals: emergency rotates can be approved by the on-call Sec eng + the owning service SRE/owner. We'll triage and set TTL.

anya: created ticket: https://company.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-7891 — included the log lines, service name, pod IDs, and a note that staging only.

devops-bot: [deploy-checker] Reminder: change requires update to k8s Secret and rollout. Use `kubectl set env` or update helm values and `helm upgrade --install`.

mike: exact commands i ran last time (staging):
```
# create new secret in Vault
vault kv put secret/staging/my-service API_KEY="newvalue"
# update k8s secret from local env (example)
kubectl -n staging set env deployment/my-service API_KEY=$(vault kv get -field=API_KEY secret/staging/my-service)
# restart to pick up new env
kubectl -n staging rollout restart deploy/my-service
# then revoke old value in Vault
vault kv delete -force secret/staging/my-service@old-version || true
```

julia: Couple extra ops notes: 1) Search logs for the key pattern and redact or remove log fragments from long-term retention (log ingestion allows deletion for the last 30d). 2) If it touched other services (i.e., used by automated jobs), rotate those credentials too. 3) Flag the rotated key in the inventory doc (Confluence) and add rotation date.

anya: who actually performs the Vault delete step? security-ops or the service owner?

security-ops: service owner (or runbook-designated oncall) performs creation/update and runtime rollout. security-ops will validate revocation and change the incident severity if needed. If HSM/KMS import needed, we coordinate with infra oncall.

mike: one more: add a short postmortem in the ticket with root cause (debug logging enabled by default on that worker) and fix the logging call to scrub envs: `LOG.debug("auth failed", mask(api_key))` — i put a PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/my-service/pull/422

anya: awesome. i'll rotate now, follow steps, paste status in the ticket, and mark for security-ops to validate. thanks all :thumbsup:

security-ops: thanks — once validated we'll close SEC-7891. If anything looks like cross‑account exposure escalate to legal/compliance per runbook.
